metas.name: Antique high roof trikes
metas.note: Found in Western Visayas, these trikes feature a passenger compartment that resembles a spaceship, with a distinctly aerodynamic design.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Bataan low roof
metas.note: Bataan has these double vertical-windowed trikes, and they’re very concentrated within Bataan
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Bicol High-Roof Trike
metas.note: The standard Bicol high-roof trike features many large, squarish windows for both driver and passenger, a large connecting window between them, and additional windows on the sides and rear. The passenger side is open and spacious.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Bicol Mid-Roof Trike
metas.note: The standard Bicol mid-roof trike shares many characteristics with the high-roof version: numerous large windows, a connecting window between driver and passenger, and a spacious passenger area.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Bohol Flat-Roof Trike
metas.note: Bohol trikes are large and boxy, with one large window and a crown. Their defining feature is an additional window located below the driver’s position.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Bohol Flat-Roof Variation
metas.note: This tuk-tuk–style trike is exclusive to Bohol. It features small horn-like mirrors at the front and small side windows. From the back, it looks fairly generic but includes two rear windows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Bukidnon Flat-Roof Trike
metas.note: Bukidnon trikes are long and distinctive, featuring a large square main window with two side windows next to it, forming a trifold layout. They often lean backward, usually have a crown on top, and may include side windows at the rear. These trikes are found in northern Mindanao and on Camiguin Island.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Calabarzon trike
metas.note: This is the standard Calabarzon trike. Key features include the padded coverings above both the passenger and driver, the curved bar in front of the driver, and the shape of the passenger car with a belt running beneath the window. There are a few minor variations in shape (such as a window above the driver, below the passenger, or differences in car size), but most of these are not strongly regional within Calabarzon. I noticed that the majority of these trikes have a silver, mirror-like, metallic finish.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Car-Looking Trike
metas.note: Very common in the Davao region and also frequent in Butuan City, these trikes resemble small cars in both shape and appearance. They are easy to recognize and come in a wide range of colors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Caraga High-Roof Trike
metas.note: Caraga trikes feature two distinct, squarish passenger windows, with a flat window beneath them. Several variations of this style exist.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Catanduanes Mid-Roof Trike
metas.note: These trikes feature square, plane-like windows and a crown on the roof. Many variations can be found within the same area.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Cebu High-Roof Pyramid Trike
metas.note: These trikes have a striking design, with a pyramid-like passenger compartment. In some cases, the window is divided into two sections.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Cebu Umbrella
metas.note: On Cebu Island, some trikes feature a roof made from fabric or tissue-like material, resembling an umbrella. This style is extremely common across the island and can be found almost everywhere.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Cotabato Flat-Roof Trike
metas.note: Cotabato trikes sometimes have a number plate mounted on the roof. They feature one or two windows that slope slightly forward, while the body beneath the windows slopes backward. The flat roof also leans backward.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Crown High-Roof Trike
metas.note: These high-roof trikes feature crowns above both the driver and passenger windows. If you see a high-roof trike with crowns, you are likely in the northern part of the country. The crown design is very distinctive, even across different body shapes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Davao Flat-Roof Trike
metas.note: This is the typical Davao City trike. It features two large windows, a bar beneath the windows, a large flat roof, and windows that slope backward. Some versions include a crown or a protruding element at the bottom (more common in downtown Davao), but the overall shape is the defining characteristic.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Davao Oriental Flat-Roof Trike
metas.note: Along the Davao Oriental coast, trikes with flat roofs and windows divided into two sections are common. A large number plate is mounted beneath the windows, and the trikes are often brightly colored.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Full leather back trike
metas.note: Similar to the leather-back trike, but with the difference that the leather also covers the roof. It can be found near Laoag City.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: General Santos High-Roof Trike
metas.note: This trike is unique to General Santos. The main window extends outward at an angle, the roof slopes forward, and the window often includes two or three horizontal lines. Beneath the main window are two small auxiliary windows. A specific shade of blue is common in downtown General Santos, while an orange variant is exclusive to Polomolok, just north of the city.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Guimaras Low-Roof Trike
metas.note: On Guimaras Island, trikes tend to have rounded or aerodynamic shapes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Isabella Low roof
metas.note: The passenger side features a hexagonal-shaped window at the rear. This type of trike is common in the northern part of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Koronadal Low-Roof Trike
metas.note: These trikes feature a long, box-shaped low roof. A crown may appear on the passenger side, and a number plate is often visible beneath a small passenger window. They appear in various colors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Lanao Mid-Roof Trike
metas.note: Trikes near Lake Lanao feature a very specific vertical passenger window and vertical bars on the passenger side. The driver’s window is more horizontal or square-shaped, and the roof is black on both sides.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Leather back Trike
metas.note: The leather-back trike can be found in the northern part of the country as well as in central Luzon, particularly in the Ilocos region. The back of the trike is easily recognizable by its black leather.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Leyte Flat-Roof Trike
metas.note: Trikes are far more common in Leyte than in Mindanao, where they tend to cluster around main roads. In Leyte, they are ubiquitous—even in rural areas. The standard Leyte trike features two slightly outward-tilting windows, a large curved crown on top, and a roof that slopes backward. The body shape beneath the windows is the easiest way to identify them
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Masbate Mid-Roof Trike
metas.note: This is the main Masbate trike design. The driver’s side is fully open with a roof, while the passenger side features a large window, a crown, metal bars, and a hexagonal shape. In Masbate City, these trikes are often yellow, though other colors exist across the region.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Mindoro Low-Roof Trike
metas.note: All Mindoro trikes share a metallic design with vivid colors. Decorative metal bars are an integral part of their overall aesthetic.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Misamis High-Roof Trike
metas.note: Common in northern Mindanao, these trikes feature airplane-style passenger windows. There are many variations, and they appear in a wide range of colors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Negros Flat-Roof Trike
metas.note: These trikes feature a curved crown on top, two windows, and a large number displayed below the passenger window. They appear in many different colors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Negros Mid-Roof Trike
metas.note: In southern Negros, mid-roof trikes share the same retro, 1970s-inspired passenger compartment design. Some versions include an additional window on the roof.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: North Cebu High-Roof Trike
metas.note: These trikes are highly distinctive, with a passenger compartment shaped somewhat like a Japanese train car. They appear in various colors and are easy to spot across Cebu Island.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: North East Cebu High-Roof Trike
metas.note: Another Cebu variant features a small horizontal window in the passenger compartment.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: North Panay High-Roof Trike
metas.note: Here’s the northern Panay trike. He’s silly & boxy, and he’s a guy, and he’s a little short don’t make fun of him.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Nueva Viscaya low roof
metas.note: The passenger side features a crown on the roof, and the trike is fitted with transparent plastic protection. These trikes are unique to this region
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Palawan Trikes
metas.note: Palawan trikes are among the most unique in the country. Their car-like shape reminiscent of a Smart car makes them immediately recognizable.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Romblon High-Roof Trike
metas.note: If you encounter unusually shaped high-roof trikes, chances are you are in the Romblon region or on Sibuyan Island.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Samar Flat-Roof Trike
metas.note: Samar flat-roof trikes have a unique curved body shape that makes them easily recognizable. They are slightly wider than average and usually feature a black roof.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Samar Mid Roof Trikes
metas.note: This type of trike that’s really small in size, has two large windows and a connecting window, and the passenger trike is very low are extremely common in Western Samar. This specific shade of red with these small details are common in Catbalogan City. These can also be identified by their silly looking singular window in the back.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: South Bukidnon Trike
metas.note: South Bukidnon trikes are generally green, with a single horizontal window and a flat roof. The roof is also green and often includes metallic crossbars.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: South Negros Flat Roof Trikes
metas.note: In southern Negros, trikes have a very distinctive design. The passenger compartment resembles a small 1970s-era car, often paired with a large square flat roof.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: South Panay Low/Mid-Roof Trike
metas.note: Southern Panay trikes feature a unique bumpy, curved body shape. The passenger window is a rounded square, and the driver’s side has no window.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Sultan Kudarat Flat-Roof Trike
metas.note: These trikes feature a large flat black roof, a small side window, and no lines on the main window. They are mainly found in Sultan Kudarat. Green versions with blue “POBLACION” text are specific to Isulan, while more colorful variants with numbers on the roof are unique to Tacurong City.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Surigao del Norte Flat-Roof Trike
metas.note: This downtown Surigao trike features an extremely long window with two or three horizontal lines, a small bumper beneath the window, and a rear bar with a side window. The roof slopes backward less than other styles, giving it a very distinct shape. These trikes appear in many different colors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Umbrella Trike
metas.note: Trikes with an umbrella-style roof can be found in the Zamboanga Peninsula and across Mindanao. These trikes are easily recognizable by their umbrella-shaped roofs. This type is common in Pagadian City and very common in Cotabato City.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Zamboanga Flat-Roof Trike
metas.note: Zamboanga City has a wide variety of trikes, but this flat-roof model is distinctive. It often features a white line separating the passenger and driver sections, horizontally shaped windows, and elaborate decorations. Zamboanga trikes are especially known for their bright, colorful designs and ornamental details.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Zamboanga High-Roof Trike
metas.note: This is essentially the only high-roof trike variant found throughout the Zamboanga Peninsula. The passenger window resembles an airplane window, the roof slopes backward, and the body slightly bulges beneath the window.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.
